tasks.title: Render de-duplicated tool guidelines deterministically in toolsNote
steps: Write TS-17-2, TS-17-3, TS-17-4 and TS-17-5 as unit tests in internal/agentrun/phase_test.go and TS-17-17 as a property test (testing/quick or a seeded math/rand generator over tool names and guideline lists with empty, whitespace and duplicate entries, comparing toolsNote(s), toolsNote(s) and toolsNote(permutation of s)); confirm they fail
In internal/agentrun/phase.go toolsNote, copy the registered slice and sort it by Name with slices.SortFunc so the guideline order matches the sorted tool-name list and never depends on input order

After the existing "Your tools are exactly: …" sentence and shell/no-shell sentence, walk the sorted tools and each tool's PromptGuidelines in declared order; strings.TrimSpace each entry, skip it when empty, and skip it when its trimmed text is already in a seen set (map used only for membership, never iterated)

When at least one guideline survives, append a newline-separated section: the heading line "Tool guidelines:" then one "- <trimmed text>" line per guideline; emit no heading when none survive (including the empty set)
Use only strings.Builder and slices; no time, randomness or map iteration in toolsNote
Run TestToolsNoteListsTheToolsAndSaysWhenThereIsNoShell and TestTS15_6_ToolsNoteListsTheSymbolTools and confirm they still pass

tasks.title: Add the search-over-execute guideline and the file-tool preference line for shell phases
steps: Write TS-17-1, TS-17-6 to TS-17-12 as unit tests in internal/agentrun/phase_test.go and TS-17-13 (SelectTools feeding toolsNote, no shell) beside the SelectTools tests in internal/agentrun/policy_test.go; confirm they fail

Check whether github.com/agentfox/agentkit-go/tools exports SearchOverExecuteGuideline (search the module cache or try compiling a reference); if it does, define searchOverExecuteGuideline = tools.SearchOverExecuteGuideline in internal/agentrun, otherwise define a local const with the text "Prefer search_files over execute+grep: it respects .gitignore and returns structured matches."
In toolsNote, compute hasShell (any registered name in ShellTools; take the first such name in sorted order as the shell name) and the set of registered names

When search_files and a shell are both registered, feed searchOverExecuteGuideline through the same trim/de-duplicate path as the declared guidelines (after the search_files tool's own guidelines) so it is emitted exactly once whether or not search_files already declares it

When a shell and at least one of read_file, search_files, find_files, list_files are registered, build one preference sentence from the clauses "Read files with `read_file`", "search with `search_files`", "find files with `find_files`", "list directories with `list_files`" in that fixed order, keeping only registered tools, joined with ", " and a final " and " (capitalise the first clause)
End the preference sentence with "; use `<shell>` only for git and for building, formatting and testing." when write_file or edit_file is registered, otherwise "; use `<shell>` only for git."
Emit the preference line after the tool-list sentence and before the "Tool guidelines:" heading; omit it when no shell or none of the four file tools is registered

Leave the existing "There is no shell: …" sentence unchanged for no-shell sets and keep SelectTools' existing execute-guideline filter so TestSelectToolsDropsExecuteGuidelinesWithoutAShell still passes

tasks.title: Make the execute description discourage reading files through the shell
steps: Write TS-17-14, TS-17-15 and TS-17-16 in internal/agentrun/policy_test.go; confirm TS-17-14 fails
In internal/agentrun/policy.go SelectTools, determine from the requested names whether read_file and/or search_files are selected

When execute is selected and at least one of them is, append to the describeForPhase output (both the read-only and writing variants) a sentence like "Do not use cat, head, tail, grep or rg to read or search repository files; use `read_file` and `search_files` instead, which respect .gitignore and return structured results.", naming only the selected built-in tools

Keep describeForPhase itself unchanged so the "The only programs allowed are: <programs>" text stays generated from the guard's programs slice, and leave the description untouched when neither read_file nor search_files is selected
Confirm TestSelectToolsTellsThePhaseItsRules still passes

tasks.title: Confirm the runner delivers the new note to the provider and the change stays in agentrun
steps: Write TS-17-18 in internal/agentrun/phase_test.go: build a Runner with the existing fauxConfig helper and a temp workspace, run a Phase with System "system", Tools read_file, search_files, execute and a Custom submit tool with PromptGuidelines ["Report by calling submit."], answer with a submit tool call, and inspect the first faux request's system prompt

Assert the prompt starts with "system" and contains "Tool guidelines:", "- Report by calling submit.", the search-over-execute text exactly once, "Read files with `read_file`" and "use `execute` only for git"

Confirm newAgent in internal/agentrun/phase.go still sets SystemPrompt to p.System plus toolsNote(registered) where registered includes the Custom submit tools; fix the wiring if submit tools are added after the note is built

Write TS-17-19 as a test in internal/agentrun (e.g. scope_test.go) that walks the non-test .go files of codefix, codeimpl, specgen, issuetriage and internal/conform (via a relative path from the package directory) and asserts none contains "Tool guidelines:", "Read files with" or the search-over-execute text, and that ReadOnlyPrograms still contains cat, head, tail, wc, rg and grep
Run go test ./internal/repomap/... and confirm the golden tests still pass without changes

tasks.title: Document the tool guidelines and file-tool preference in the CLI and model-usage docs
steps: Write TS-17-20 as a root-level test docs_tool_guidelines_test.go (package matching the other docs_*_test.go files) that extracts the "What the model may and may not do" section of docs/cli.md and reads docs/model-usage.md, asserting each contains "Tool guidelines", "search_files" and "git"; confirm it fails

In docs/cli.md "What the model may and may not do", explain that the system prompt ends with a tools note listing the tools, a "Tool guidelines:" section with every registered tool's guidelines (including submit_* tools), and, in phases with a shell, a line telling the model to read with read_file, search with search_files, find with find_files and list with list_files, using execute only for git (and for building, formatting and testing in writing phases); mention the execute description's added sentence

Run make check and confirm it exits 0
